meta.purpose: Worked instances of the chemistry mapping, found by search over ATOMS.md rather than composed as examples.

method.isomers: entries whose recipes reduce to an identical ingredient set
method.catalysts: entries whose definition says survives / without being consumed / its own
method.cycles: entries whose recipe names an entry whose recipe names them back
method.functional_groups: recipes sharing an ingredient where the qualifier fixes the outcome

members.name: Melt
members.definition: solid becomes liquid

members.name: Freeze
members.definition: liquid becomes solid

members.name: Boil
members.definition: liquid becomes gas

members.name: Condense
members.definition: gas becomes liquid

members.name: Sublimate
members.definition: solid becomes gas directly

members.name: Fall
members.definition: an unsupported thing drops

members.name: Lever
members.definition: a rigid bar turning about a point

members.name: Predict
members.definition: infer the next state from the last

members.name: Associate
members.definition: link events because one precedes the other

members.name: Expand
members.definition: heating grows volume

members.name: Contract
members.definition: cooling shrinks it

members.name: Queue
members.definition: first in, first out

members.name: Stack
members.definition: last in, first out

members.name: Attraction
members.definition: massive things pull

members.name: Bound system
members.definition: many bodies held together

members.name: Remnant radiation
members.definition: leftover signal from the beginning

members.name: Rapid early expansion
members.definition: a brief period of very fast growth

members.name: Recurse
members.definition: apply the same solution inside itself

members.name: Recurse
members.definition: apply the same solution inside itself — also Information T4

members.name: Cotard delusion
members.definition: The extreme feeling of not being "in" one's body, or believing one is dead. Used for critical system failure states.

members.name: Dissociation
members.definition: The feeling of watching yourself from outside. Actions happen, but you don't feel like the author. A trap state.

members.name: Brittle failure
members.definition: A material with low fracture toughness shatters instantly with no plastic deformation (glass, ceramic).

members.name: Crack propagation
members.definition: A microscopic flaw (crack) concentrates stress at its tip. The crack grows uncontrollably if the material is brittle.

members.name: Work harden
members.definition: Repeated plastic deformation (hammering) increases hardness but decreases ductility. The material becomes stiffer until it cracks.

members.name: Perfect plasticity
members.definition: A material that deforms without any resistance once yield is exceeded. It flows like honey.

members.name: Shear failure
members.definition: Forces slide one layer of material against another. Rivets snap, glue peels, beams twist.

members.name: Decohesion
members.definition: Molecules are pulled apart at the atomic level. The material separates along grain boundaries. The ultimate limit of all materials.

members.name: Lens
members.definition: A curved transparent medium. Converging (convex) focuses light; diverging (concave) spreads it.

members.name: Acoustic lens
members.definition: A curved medium that focuses or defocuses sound waves. Like a lens, but for pressure waves.

members.name: Rhythm entrain
members.definition: Align your actions to an external beat. Move in time with the metronome.

members.name: Clock skew
members.definition: Two clocks are out of sync. Events happen at different times for different observers.

members.name: Counterplay
members.definition: A strategy that is specifically designed to defeat another strategy. Rock-paper-scissors.

members.name: Balance
members.definition: No strategy is dominant. All viable strategies have roughly equal winning potential.

members.name: Telegraph
members.definition: An action that signals your future action. A "tell" that can be exploited.

members.name: Baiting
members.definition: Deliberately perform a suboptimal action to lure the opponent into a trap.

members.name: Gambler fallacy
members.definition: Believing that a streak of heads makes tails more likely. The "law of small numbers."

members.name: Hot hand
members.definition: Believing that a streak of successes makes future successes more likely.

members.name: Minimax
members.definition: Choose the strategy that maximizes your minimum possible payoff. Play it safe.

members.name: Maximax
members.definition: Choose the strategy that maximizes your maximum possible payoff. Go for the jackpot.

members.name: Proactive interf
members.definition: Old memories interfere with the retrieval of new ones.

members.name: Retroactive interf
members.definition: New memories interfere with the retrieval of old ones.

members.name: State dependence
members.definition: Memory retrieval is best when the internal state (mood, drug) matches the encoding state.

members.name: Déjà vu
members.definition: The feeling of having experienced a present situation before, without a specific memory.

members.name: Flow engage
members.definition: Enter a state of total immersion. The action becomes effortless.

members.name: Flow challenge
members.definition: Continuously adjust the challenge to stay in the flow channel. Never bored, never anxious.

members.name: Negative loop
members.definition: Compare current state to setpoint. If error exists, apply correction to reduce it. Stabilizes.

members.name: The control hierarchy
members.definition: A multi-level system where higher-level setpoints shape lower-level behavior. A chain of command.

members.name: Level ascend
members.definition: Move from a lower level of reality to a higher one. Ascend the ontological hierarchy.

members.name: Level descend
members.definition: Move from a higher level of reality to a lower one. Descend the ontological hierarchy.

members.name: Pull
members.definition: Move an object closer to the actor.

members.name: Push
members.recipe: Grab (or contact) + Move (away from self) + Sustained_Exertion
members.definition: Move an object away from the actor.

members.name: Climb
members.definition: Ascending a vertical surface using handholds.

members.name: Swing
members.definition: Move an object or self in an arc.

members.name: Binary choice
members.definition: The simplest form of choice: yes/no, left/right, A/B. The fundamental fork.

members.name: Multiple choice
members.definition: A choice among multiple alternatives (A, B, C, D...).

members.name: Hesitation
members.definition: A choice that takes a long time because the options are equally preferred or the basis is unclear.

members.name: Decision fatigue
members.definition: The progressive degradation of decision quality after many choices. Energy is depleted.

members.name: Deduce
members.definition: Draw a specific conclusion from general premises. If all A are B, and C is A, then C is B.

members.name: Reasoning chain
members.definition: A sequence of logical steps from premise to conclusion. The "chain" of reasoning.

members.name: Loop
members.definition: The fundamental habit unit. A stimulus triggers an action that yields a reward.

members.name: Habit stack
members.definition: Chaining multiple habits together. One habit triggers the next.

members.name: Buy
members.definition: Acquiring a resource by giving currency. The "purchase."

members.name: Sell
members.definition: Giving a resource in exchange for currency. The "sale."

members.name: Descend
members.definition: The act of falling asleep. The crossing of the threshold.

members.name: Ascend
members.definition: The act of waking up. The return to the conscious world.

members.name: Connect
members.definition: The fundamental act of network construction. Creating a link.

members.name: Traverse
members.definition: Moving through a network. The "pathfinding."

members.name: Mastery
members.definition: The state of complete, integrated mastery. The "expert."

members.name: The mastery path
members.definition: The path to mastery. The "way of the expert."

members.name: Craft
members.definition: The skilled creation of objects or outcomes.

members.name: The craftsman
members.definition: The archetype of the one who creates through skill.

catalysts.name: Producer
catalysts.definition: makes its own energy, stays put

catalysts.name: Self-organised criticality
catalysts.definition: it finds the edge without being tuned there

catalysts.name: Self-sustaining rhythm
catalysts.definition: oscillates at its own rate, independent of what drives it

catalysts.name: Catalysis
catalysts.definition: a cheaper route to the same end, and the helper survives

catalysts.name: Autocatalysis
catalysts.definition: the product speeds its own production — Dynamic `Positive feedback` is the same shape

catalysts.name: Self-assembly
catalysts.definition: units organise into a larger structure without being placed

catalysts.name: Priming
catalysts.definition: exposure shapes later responses without being noticed

catalysts.name: Witness stance
catalysts.definition: observe your own reasoning without being it — the independence clause applied to yourself

catalysts.name: Trans shipment
catalysts.definition: A resource passes through an intermediate node without being processed. A relay.

catalysts.name: Over-attribution of agency
catalysts.definition: Treat an object as if it has a will. It may act on its own if properly respected/provoked.

catalysts.name: Ultra stability
catalysts.definition: A system that can maintain stability even when its internal structure changes. It adapts its own setpoints.

catalysts.name: The infinite regulator
catalysts.definition: A system that regulates its own regulation. It has a setpoint for its setpoint. Infinite regress.

catalysts.name: The homeostatic universe
catalysts.definition: The universe itself is a homeostatic system. It maintains its own constants (fine-tuning).

catalysts.name: The autopoietic
catalysts.definition: A system that produces itself. It maintains its own identity by regenerating its components.

catalysts.name: Poetic function
catalysts.definition: Language is used for its own sake. Poetry, wordplay, rhythm, and beauty.

catalysts.name: Starvation response
catalysts.definition: The system breaks down its own tissues (muscle, fat) for energy and downregulates non-essential processes.

catalysts.name: Mirroring
catalysts.definition: The immediate recognition that the Other is like me: a subject with its own interiority.

catalysts.name: The dream ecosystem
catalysts.definition: The complete, interconnected world of a dream. Its own ecology.

catalysts.name: Self modifying
catalysts.definition: An automaton that can modify its own rules. The "self-programming."

members.name: Runaway
members.definition: growth with nothing to stop it

members.name: Positive feedback
members.definition: the response increases it

momentum.name: Ascent
momentum.definition: error shrinking under correction; the trajectory that ends in a win

momentum.name: Descent
momentum.definition: error growing because nothing corrects it; the trajectory that ends in a loss

momentum.name: Acoustic radiation pressure
momentum.definition: Sound carries momentum. It can push objects. An acoustic tractor beam.

res.name: Stress
res.recipe: Stim high + Res depleting + Damp overloaded
res.definition: pushing against a constraint while running down

res.name: Urgency
res.definition: time pressure shortening how much gets searched before acting. Not downstream of desire — `Frustration resp = Frust + Blockage`, so urgency needs wanting AND being unable

res.name: Stalemate
res.definition: two forces exactly balanced; nothing moves

res.name: Runaway
res.definition: growth with nothing to stop it

res.name: Stagnation
res.definition: error neither shrinking nor growing while the budget runs down; the trajectory that ends in a draw

res.name: Consumption
res.definition: the final use; the resource is gone

res.name: Public good
res.definition: nobody can be kept out and use does not deplete it

res.name: Liquidity
res.definition: how easily a thing converts without losing value

res.name: Synchronize
res.definition: The alignment of two systems through sympathetic vibration.

res.name: Resonate
res.definition: The amplification of connection through alignment of frequency.

res.name: Sympathetic bond
res.definition: A connection that persists across distance. Sympathetic magic.

res.name: Resonance field
res.definition: A field of resonance where all connected nodes vibrate together.

damp.name: Rest
damp.recipe: Stim low + Var low + Damp high
damp.definition: stable, unchanging, unresponsive; nothing happens unless provoked

damp.name: Stress
damp.recipe: Stim high + Res depleting + Damp overloaded
damp.definition: pushing against a constraint while running down

damp.name: Setpoint [dup: `Goal`, Desire]
damp.definition: the reference a system compares its state against; the thing error is measured from. Cybernetic says it directly — `Goal seeking = Setpoint + Error + Action + Feedback`

damp.name: Break habit
damp.definition: inject noise while watching, and dissipate the momentum — a brake, and `Damp` exists in Dynamic, Acoustic and Cybernetic already

damp.name: Negative feedback
damp.definition: the response reduces the thing that caused it

damp.name: Reverberation
damp.definition: The persistence of sound after the source stops. Long reverberation = "live" room. Short = "dead" room.

damp.name: Absorption
damp.definition: A material that soaks up sound energy (acoustic foam, carpet). Reduces reflections.

damp.name: Damping material
damp.definition: A material engineered to absorb specific frequencies. Makes rooms acoustically "dead."

damp.name: Vibration sensing
damp.definition: Detect vibrations through solid contact. A "thump" on the floor can be felt through the structure.

damp.name: Gain tune
damp.definition: Adjust the gain to achieve the desired response: fast without overshoot, stable without sluggishness.

positive feedback.name: Runaway
positive feedback.definition: growth with nothing to stop it

positive feedback.name: Descent
positive feedback.definition: error growing because nothing corrects it; the trajectory that ends in a loss

negative feedback.name: Ascent
negative feedback.definition: error shrinking under correction; the trajectory that ends in a win

negative feedback.name: Self-sustaining rhythm
negative feedback.definition: oscillates at its own rate, independent of what drives it
